works.title: Adsorptive Membranes for PFAS Removal: Current Status, Design Principles, and Research Needs
institutions: Rice University
works.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are contaminants of concern due to their persistence, occurrence in natural waters, and association with adverse health outcomes. Producing potable water from PFAS-impacted sources requires selectively removing PFAS from complex waters. Adsorptive membranes are an emerging strategy for PFAS removal due to their tunable architectures and chemistries, modularity, and high water permeances. However, it is difficult to compare adsorptive membrane performance across studies and identify membrane properties governing PFAS removal due to the diversity of materials, architectures, testing conditions, and reported performance metrics. This review critically evaluates the state of PFAS adsorptive membranes by examining nanofiber membranes, asymmetric membranes, adsorptive nanofiltration (NF) membranes, and ion exchange membranes used for adsorptive PFAS removal. We highlight structure-property-performance relationships, assess current testing strategies, and recommend standard performance metrics to enable cross-study comparisons. We further compare adsorptive membrane performance to conventional reverse osmosis (RO) and NF membranes. Finally, we apply the convection-diffusion-adsorption (CDA) model to published PFAS breakthrough data to gain mechanistic insights into the role of membrane properties and operating parameters on PFAS removal. Overall, this review provides a framework for evaluating adsorptive membranes, identifies key research gaps, and establishes design criteria to advance adsorptive PFAS separations.

works.title: Cyclic dipeptide reaction-induced in situ self-assembly interfacial polymerization for high-flux organic solvent nanofiltration polyamide membranes
works.abstract: Rapid, disordered network formation during interfacial polymerization (IP) broadens the pore-size distribution of polyamide organic solvent nanofiltration membranes, limiting both permeance and sieving precision. Here, we developed a reaction-induced self-assembly strategy using diamino cyclic dipeptide monomers and trimesoyl chloride (TMC). Amidation is proposed to increase the amphiphilicity of nascent oligomers, while intermolecular hydrogen bonding promotes local organization and suppresses disordered network formation. Model reactions, transmission electron microscopy, and grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering supported reaction-induced short-range ordering. The optimized LL-TMC membrane exhibited a narrow pore-size distribution centered at 0.82 nm and a methanol permeance of 40.8 ± 1.4 L·bar−1·h−1·m−2. It sharply distinguished Congo red (697 Da) from Solvent Red 43 (648 Da), with rejections of 95.3 ± 1.5% and 24.5 ± 6.1%, respectively, and separated both dyes in a mixed-solute system. This study indicates that regulating the local structural evolution during IP through monomer molecular design is a feasible approach to optimizing the pore size distribution of polyamide membranes and achieving synergistic enhancement of high permeance and high sieving precision.

works.title: Desalinated wastewater for aquaponic reuse: challenge and impact
institutions: Centre de Recherches et des Technologies des Eaux
National Institute of Applied Science and Technology
RWTH Aachen University
works.abstract: This study looked into whether it’s possible and safe to use treated and desalinated municipal wastewater in a pilot aquaponics system. This system combined Nile tilapia fish with three growing. Deep-water culture (DWC), nutrient film technique (NFT), and grow beds. The wastewater went through several stages: an aerated moving bed biofilm reactor, a constructed wetland, sand and activated-carbon filters, and finally nanofiltration-reverse osmosis. This treatment removed 44% of COD, 95.6% of ammonia, and 33% of phosphate. The nanofiltration step removed about two-thirds of bivalent dissolved salts, 57% of sodium, 45% of chloride, and 39% of nitrates. Some micropollutants were removed, by 66%. During the experiment, the aquaponic water had an electrical coductivity between 0.5 and 2.2 mS/cm, a pH from 6.0 to 8.3, and a temperature ranging from 14 to 29 °C. All the fish survived, and their average daily weight gain was 1.97 g/day in Tank 1 and 0.86 and 1.26 g/day in Tank 2. The DWC, NFT, and grow beds successfully grew lettuce, cauliflower, endive, mint, basil, strawberry, tomato, fennel, and pepper. Tests found no Salmonella in the water, fish, or crops. However, some substances were still present in the DWC water, including benzotriazole (32.7 ng/L), carbamazepine (68.9 ng/L), and metoprolol (12 ng/L). The plants had nitrogen content between 0.18% and 0.41%, and their levels of phenol, sugar, proline, and phosphorus indicated good nutritional quality. In summary, using membrane-based treatment allowed the reuse of wastewater for aquaponics. However, it’s important to keep monitoring for nutrient imbalances and any leftover micropollutants.

works.title: Electronic Polarization of Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
works.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
institutions: Southeast University
Southeast University , , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy. This unique pore environment promotes the uptake and transport of polar solvents, while enhancing separation selectivity by retarding highly polar solutes through polarity-dependent solute-framework interactions. Furthermore, the low surface energy imparted by the robust C–F bonds also reduces irreversible foulant adhesion and facilitates permeance recovery after cleaning. The resultant COF membrane achieves a molecular weight cutoff down to 350 Da and stable operation for over 550 h. Notably, it differentiates structurally related fluoroquinolone antibiotics according to their molecular polarity and delivers a favorable separation factor of 8.9 for norfloxacin over its synthetic intermediate piperazine. This work demonstrates that engineering pore-wall polarity in COF membranes provides a viable route to chemically regulated molecular recognition beyond size-based separation.

works.title: Mesophase-Derived Polymer Membranes with Precisely Defined Pores for Molecular and Ion Separations
institutions: Tohoku University
University of Pennsylvania
Tohoku University , , ,
University of Pennsylvania , , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Polymer membranes are central components in critical technologies, including energy generation and storage, water purification, and chemical separations. There are pressing needs for membranes that transport uncharged and charged molecular, or ionic species, with bespoke selectivity and high permeability in these technological areas, including the growing need for efficient critical mineral separations and resource recovery. For these and other challenging molecular or ionic separations, the focus is on membranes with 1 nm scale (0.5–2 nm) pores that can offer both size- and affinity-based mechanisms for separation. This perspective discusses the current state of the art in nanoporous polymer membranes and reviews recent progress toward the realization of ideal membranes for such separations—i.e., membranes with uniform, continuous, and precisely defined pores at the 1 nm length scale. Emphasis is placed on materials derived from molecular self-assembly, particularly lyotropic mesophases formed from amphiphilic monomers that can be crosslinked to produce monolithic membranes with well-defined, continuous transport pathways. These materials represent a potentially important advance given their attractive separation performance, and the versatility with which their properties can be modified. Developments in fabrication, pore shape, and pore chemistry control are discussed, along with opportunities to address important contemporary and emerging applications.

works.title: Decoupling Ion Selectivity and Transport via Dual-Scale Interlayer Nanochannels in Reduced Graphene Oxide Membranes for Lithium Separation
institutions: Ajou University
Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute
Korea University of Science and Technology
Kongju National University
Ajou University , , ,
Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute (KERI) , , ,
University of Science and Technology (UST) , , ,
Kongju National University , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Selective separation of Li+ from coexisting Ni2+, Co2+, and Mn2+ is an important step in lithium recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) membranes offer a promising platform for this separation through their ångström-scale interlayer nanochannels. However, the same narrow nanochannels hinder ion diffusion, inducing a severe permeability–selectivity trade-off. To decouple ion selectivity from transport, we report a nanoconfined sol–gel strategy for constructing a dual-scale interlayer architecture in rGO membranes. Intercalated between graphene oxide layers, aluminosilicate (AS) sols serve as cross-linkers and in situ vapor sources. During thermal aging, sol–gel condensation generates vapor that expands un-cross-linked galleries into transport highways, while cross-linked domains retain ion-selective confinement. The architecture is tunable across ion-selective interlayer spacing (dS, 7.1–8.3 Å) and expanded interlayer spacing (dE, 34–94 Å). Compared with conventional rGO membranes, the optimized dual-scale spacing membrane increases Li+ permeability 5.4-fold in mixed-ion solution while achieving high divalent-ion selectivity (Li+/Ni2+ = 246, Li+/Co2+ = 391, Li+/Mn2+ = 448). Molecular dynamics simulations attribute this selectivity to asymmetric energy barriers imposed on Li+ and divalent cations within the cross-linked spacing, while the expanded spacing facilitates low-resistance transport. This work shows how nanoconfined sol–gel chemistry can open a design space for fabricating high-performance ion recovery membranes.

works.title: Low-Cost Graphene–Cellulose Membranes Prepared by Vacuum Filtration for Low-Pressure Brackish Water Treatment
works.abstract: This study presents the development of a low-cost graphene oxide (GO)–cellulose membrane fabricated via vacuum-assisted filtration for low-pressure brackish water treatment. Among the investigated nanocarbon–solvent systems, the GO–NMP membrane exhibited the best overall combination of coating stability and salt-rejection performance and was therefore selected for detailed transport experiments. The membrane achieved a maximum salt rejection of 10.24 ± 0.19% at 2.97 g L?¹ NaCl (n = 5), while water flux and membrane permeance exhibited distinct non-linear behaviour within the investigated salinity range. The reproducible rejection extremum and coupled transport trends suggest an apparent salinity-dependent transport region, potentially associated with GO swelling, charge screening, and changes in lamellar transport pathways. Water flux increased with operating pressure, whereas membrane permeance decreased, consistent with increasing hydraulic resistance under compression. Although the salt rejection remained insufficient for stand-alone desalination, the simple fabrication procedure makes the GO–cellulose membrane a useful platform for low-pressure brackish-water treatment studies and further membrane optimization.

works.title: Carbon Nanomembranes as Precision Platforms for Subnanometer Molecular and Ionic Transport
institutions: Hebei Petroleum University of Technology
Bielefeld University
Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Guangzhou)
Department of Chemical Engineering, Hebei Petroleum University of Technology, Chengde 067000, China
Faculty of Physics, Bielefeld University, 33615 Bielefeld, Germany
Guangdong Basic Research Center of Excellence for Ecological Security and Green Development, Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Guangzhou), Guangzhou 511458, China
works.abstract: Carbon nanomembranes (CNMs) are an emerging class of ultrathin carbon sheets with intrinsic sub–nanometer porosity and chemically programmable interfaces. Unlike other two–dimensional (2D) membranes, CNMs uniquely combine molecular–scale thickness, high pore density, and large–area scalability, enabling a transport regime that approaches the selectivity and efficiency of biological channels while retaining the robustness of synthetic materials. In this perspective, we argue that CNMs constitute a versatile platform for precision transport of water, gases, and ions. We first introduce a structural design toolkit that links precursor chemistry, cross–linking conditions, and support architecture to tunable parameters such as thickness. We then discuss the underlying transport physics in sub–nanometer CNM channels, highlighting single–file water permeation, adsorption–diffusion–controlled transport, and hydration–shell–mediated ion sieving. On this basis, we revisit CNM applications, ultrafast water permeation, gas sieving, and ion discrimination, not as isolated case studies, but as demonstrations of a unified design principle: controlling molecular structure and interfacial chemistry at the angstrom scale to engineer function. Finally, we outline key challenges and opportunities, including defect management, scalable fabrication, and integration into device architectures. By combining sub–nanometer confinement, molecular–scale thickness, and tunable interfacial chemistry, CNMs offer a synthetic platform for exploring transport principles relevant to biological channels and developing membrane devices for separation and energy storage.

works.title: Construction of Self-Assembled Nanofiltration Membranes Based on TA/PEI Interlayer and Performance Study
institutions: Zhejiang Sci-Tech University

works.abstract: To overcome the chemical inertness of polyethersulfone (PES) flat-sheet membrane surfaces and expand their application in printing and dyeing wastewater filtration, a PES flat-sheet membrane was prepared as a support membrane using PES as the membrane-forming polymer and zinc oxide (ZnO) as the modifier. A tannic acid/polyethyleneimine (TA/PEI) interlayer was constructed on the support membrane via co-deposition. Polyethyleneimine/sodium alginate (PEI/SA) polyelectrolyte multilayers were then self-assembled layer-by-layer on the interlayer. A self-assembled composite nanofiltration membrane was also prepared. SEM, AFM, FTIR, XPS, a water contact angle goniometer, and a cross-flow filtration apparatus were used to study the effects of the TA/PEI mass ratio and deposition time on the micromorphology, chemical composition, hydrophilicity, separation performance, and stability of the nanofiltration membrane. The results show that, at a TA/PEI mass ratio of 1:1 and a deposition time of 2 h, the interlayer completely covered the substrate and provided stable chemical anchoring sites for subsequent layer-by-layer (LbL) self-assembly. The resulting T1P1-2-L4 nanofiltration membrane has a water contact angle of 47.6 degrees, an average roughness of 14.5 nm, and a separation layer thickness of about 78.6 nm. Filtration tests show that the membrane rejects more than 97.4% of Rhodamine B, crystal violet, Congo red, and acid fuchsin. Its permeate flux ranges from 40.5 to 48.2 L·m−2·h−1. After 24 h of continuous operation, the rejection of the Congo red solution remains above 99.3%. The flux decline is only 8.56%. From 6 to 24 h, the flux remains stable at about 38.5 L·m−2·h−1. The membrane shows good short-term operational stability. This work provides a theoretical basis for preparing high-performance and stable nanofiltration membranes.

works.abstract: Traffic energy harvesting has been studied almost exclusively for electricity, and no transient model couples the full mechanical-to-hydraulic chain of a speed bump that pressurizes brackish water for reverse osmosis while treating the wheel–bump contact as a unilateral constraint. This work formulates such a model: half-car dynamics with pitch, a unilaterally constrained speed bump, four single-acting pistons with check-valve rectification, a hydropneumatic accumulator with adiabatic charge and isothermal discharge, and a solution-diffusion RO element with emergent recovery. The contact law transmits to the platform only the compressive tire load, the static axle load minus the dynamic extension, which is also the lift-off threshold; the tire spring of the vehicle model remains bilateral and the effect of that asymmetry is bounded. An event-driven Runge–Kutta scheme converges at first order; a nine-step study of the reference event shows every reported quantity within 0.7% of its limit; the model is verified but not experimentally validated. For a 10,500 kg vehicle at 30 km/h, the tires deliver 8.98 kJ and the accumulator stores 8.03 kJ (89.3%); the end stop takes 1.5%. The platform is driven by the static axle load and the lighter axle bounds the design. The event pumps 3.58 L and yields 1.21 L of permeate at 1.81 kWh/m3 and 788 mg/L from a 16.7 g/L feed. Across six commercial modules selectivity, not water permeability, sets product quality; a 1 km/h sweep without clipping shows weak speed sensitivity and a re-impact band at 14 to 20 km/h. The objective is to demonstrate by numerical modeling that the chain works and where it loses energy. At about one liter of non-potable water per vehicle the production is limited; competitiveness with conventional desalination has not been established, and the model includes no techno-economic assessment.

works.title: Tailoring hydrophobic <scp>PDMS</scp> – <scp>PVDF</scp> membranes via solvent–polymer compatibility and additives for membrane distillation desalination
works.journal: The Canadian Journal of Chemical Engineering
institutions: Department of Chemical Engineering Malaviya National Institute of Technology Jaipur Jaipur India
Department of Chemical Engineering Sardar Vallabhbhai National Institute of Technology Surat Surat India
works.abstract: Abstract Membrane wetting and limited operational stability remain major challenges in membrane distillation, and both are strongly influenced by solvent selection and phase‐inversion behaviour. In this study, the polymer–solvent compatibility of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) was evaluated using Hansen solubility parameter (HSP) distance analysis to guide the fabrication of solution‐blended PDMS–PVDF membranes. Four solvents—NMP, DMF, DMSO, and THF—were investigated. The HSP results indicated that NMP and DMF are compatible with PVDF, while THF exhibited stronger affinity for PDMS. Accordingly, PVDF was dissolved in NMP and DMF, and PDMS in THF. Additives, including PEG‐400, H 3 PO 4 , and toluene, were incorporated. NMP‐based membranes demonstrated higher hydrophobicity, with the PEG‐400‐modified membrane exhibiting a water contact angle of 104.3°, compared to 83.9° for the DMF‐based system. Membrane porosity ranged from 51.42% to 57.8%. AFM analysis revealed maximum surface roughness (Ra = 5.554 nm; Sq = 7.389 nm) for the PEG‐400‐modified membrane. SEM, XRD, and FTIR analyses confirmed favourable morphology and structural characteristics. During VMD desalination of a 20,000 mg L −1 NaCl solution, the permeate flux decreased from 18.5 to 17.6 kg m −2 h −1 over 180 h, while salt rejection remained approximately 99.77%. The selected membrane exhibited an LEP of approximately 294.5 kPa and a maximum thermal efficiency of 93.70%. The integration of HSP‐guided solvent screening, controlled additive comparison, solution blending, and long‐term VMD validation distinguishes this work from conventional solvent‐screening studies.

institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing synthetic membranes that can autonomously adapt their ion selectivity in response to ambient mechanical energy remains a longstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale piezoelectric gating mechanism in an artificial PIEZO channel constructed from a piezoelectric MXene membrane, which harnesses ambient mechanical energy—from ultrasound to fluid flow—to power mechano‑adaptive and highly selective ion transport. Through molecular engineering of an MXene framework, we concurrently stabilize sub‑nanometer channels and amplify intrinsic piezoelectricity. Under ultrasound, the generated piezoelectric field at the sub‑nanometer scale orchestrates a reversible ‘size–charge’ sieving process, achieving exceptional K + /Mg 2+ selectivity (>180), approximately nine‐fold that of traditional pressure‐driven membranes. Combining molecular dynamics simulations, in situ characterization, and theoretical analysis, we reveal that the piezoelectric field preferentially dehydrates weakly hydrated K + ions while imposing valence‐dependent electrostatic barriers on multivalent Mg 2+ , enabling selective K + transport. Crucially, we establish that the efficacy of this mechano‐adaptive response scales linearly with the material's intrinsic piezoelectric coefficient—a quantitative correlation validated across diverse material systems. This work provides a nanoscale mechanistic understanding of piezoelectric gating in sub‑nanometer channels and establishes a quantitative correlation between the piezoelectric coefficient and selective ion transport, offering a mechanistic foundation for the design of mechano‐responsive membranes.

works.title: Hierarchically structured PVDF/Graphene Oxide-Nanodiamond nanofibrous membranes with enhanced wettability and Oil/Water separation
institutions: University of Mazandaran
works.abstract: Oil-in-water emulsion separation remains challenging because membranes must combine suitable wettability, high separation efficiency, and resistance to fouling. In this study, electrospun PVDF nanofibrous membranes incorporating graphene oxide-nanodiamond (GO-ND) nanohybrids were developed for oily wastewater treatment. The optimized membrane exhibited a hierarchical fibrous morphology and improved surface wettability, with the water contact angle decreasing from approximately 143° for pristine PVDF to 71°, while the underwater oil contact angle increased from 27° to 106°. Incorporation of 0.75 wt% GO–ND also improved the mechanical properties, increasing tensile strength from 4.27 to 7.81 MPa and elongation at break from 24.2% to 37.9%. Under gravity-driven filtration, the optimized membrane achieved fluxes of 367, 350, and 299 LMH, with oil rejection efficiencies of 96.11%, 97.12%, and 94.24% for hexane-, toluene-, and motor-oil-in-water emulsions, respectively. For surfactant-stabilized toluene emulsions, fluxes of 273.8 and 256 LMH were obtained with sodium dodecyl sulfate and Tween 80, respectively. After 20 filtration cycles, the membrane retained approximately 87.5% of its initial flux and 94% of its initial oil rejection. These results highlight the effectiveness of GO-ND nanohybrids in enhancing membrane wettability, mechanical robustness, and separation efficiency for oily wastewater treatment.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH‐dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100‐fold NaCl gradient and pH 1/13 polarization, they deliver 20.2 W m − 2 . Experiments verify pH‐dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH‐mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

The results show that this hybrid structure is a precise, selective, flexible, and mechanically stable biomimetic filtration system.

works.abstract: Abstract Developing ultrathin, highly selective membranes that emulate biological ion channels is a primary goal of synthetic membrane technology. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising platform for constructing subnanometer fluidic channels, simultaneously achieving high permeance and excellent selectivity in 2D ionic membranes remains a significant challenge. This bottleneck originates from the complexities involved in controlling the precise structural arrangement within nanosheet assemblies. In this work, we demonstrate that the atomic-layer ordering of 2D van der Waals (vdW) ion channels is a decisive factor in achieving ultrathin, highly selective membranes. By assembling 2D titania nanosheets with atomic layer-by-layer regularity, we fabricate atomic stacking membranes (ASMs) that achieve near-unity ion selectivity within an ultrathin (∼50 nm) framework. The structural regularity of these ASMs causes continuous overlap of the electrical double layer throughout the 2D ion channels, facilitating robust electrostatic regulation and maximizing selectivity. The result is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Leveraging the “Lego-like” modular assembly advantage of ASMs, we demonstrate multifunctional heterostructural iontronic devices and gate-controlled iontronic transistors featuring on/off ratios up to 104. Furthermore, the well-ordered 2D ion channels within these ASMs enable high-performance osmotic energy harvesting. This solution-processable atomic-layer van der Waals assembly strategy for ultrathin and highly selective ASMs establishes a versatile platform for uniformly regulating 2D angstrom-scale ion transport, paving the way for advanced biomimetic iontronics and efficient energy conversion.

works.abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporators provide a promising pathway for sustainable desalination and resource recovery from hypersaline brines, yet their performance is often limited by inefficient interfacial energy utilization and salt crystallization fouling. Although interfacial water-state regulation and charged-interface-mediated salt management have been explored separately, their coupled physicochemical interactions remain insufficiently understood. Multiscale channels were fabricated by in situ Schiff-base polymerization of electrospun membranes to increase the fraction of intermediate water and immobilize sulfonate groups for Donnan-effect-mediated ion regulation. This coupled structure–charge design promotes vapor generation while alleviating interfacial salt accumulation at the evaporation surface. The resulting evaporator achieves stable evaporation rates exceeding 1.30 kg m −2 h −1 in 15 wt% brines over nine consecutive 12 h cycles under 1 sun irradiation, reaching 2.04 kg m −2 h −1 under reduced pressure. This work provides a mechanistic bridge between nanoconfinement, water-state regulation and Donnan-effect-mediated ion redistribution, providing a design principle for durable solar desalination and brine concentration under hypersaline conditions.

works.abstract: Abstract Polysiloxane membranes are among the most attractive candidates for gas separation; however, their fabrication remains challenging due to the two-to-three-orders-of-magnitude mismatch between the pore size of the support, typically in the sub-micrometer to micrometer range, and the size of sol particles, which often necessitates complex multilayer structures. In this study, we propose a strategy to overcome this limitation, termed “molecular-net transfer”. This strategy employs micrometer-sized sol particles to prevent penetration into the porous support. Subsequent heat treatment induces relaxation of the gel particles, promoting their coalescence and resulting in the direct formation of a uniform polysiloxane layer without a conventional nanoporous intermediate layer. The resulting membrane exhibited an H2 permeance as high as 5.6 × 10−7 mol m−2 s−1 Pa−1 with an H2/SF6 permeance ratio of 2600, demonstrating the simultaneous achievement of simple fabrication and size-sieving-based high permselectivity. Notably, the chemical structure and sub-nanometer network of the dried gel were largely preserved during heat treatment, despite macroscopic transformation from discrete particles to a continuous film. This feature enables the direct transfer of pre-organized pore structures into the final membrane, offering a new strategy for controlling microstructure in molecular-sieving membranes.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Ion‐exchange membranes offer a promising route for osmotic energy conversion from salinity gradients, yet their performance is often limited by the balance between ion selectivity and ionic conductivity within nanoconfined channels. Here, we develop thermally regulated poly(sodium 4‐styrenesulfonate)/aramid nanofiber (PSS/ANF) membranes through a dual‐regulation strategy combining polyelectrolyte incorporation and controlled thermal treatment. The incorporation of negatively charged PSS enriches fixed sulfonate groups and modulates the interfibrillar nanochannel environment, while moderate thermal treatment further adjusts the PSS/ANF network structure and confined‐water mobility. This combined regulation creates tunable nanofibrous channels with adjusted interfacial charge environments. As a result, electrokinetic performance exhibits a non‐monotonic dependence on PSS content and thermal treatment, revealing that nanoconfined channels inherently require a balanced configuration between charge density, channel connectivity, and ionic conductivity. The optimized 150H‐25PANF membrane delivers a power density of 5.7 W m −2 under a 50‐fold KCl gradient and 3.8 W m −2 under a 0.5 M/0.01 M NaCl gradient. Under a 400‐fold KCl gradient at 50°C, the power density further increases to 29.8 W m −2 . These findings demonstrate that nanoconfinement engineering provides an effective pathway to regulate confined‐water mobility and interfacial ion transport simultaneously, offering a general design framework for high‐performance osmotic energy conversion.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Ion‐selective membranes are widely employed to extract energy and resources from seawater, yet their performance is significantly compromised by divalent ions present in natural seawater. Here, we present a graphene oxide‐based monovalent cation‐selective membrane with high ion selectivity and permeability that can reject divalent ions by leveraging steric exclusion within nanoconfined interlayers. The graphene oxide nanochannels are dual‐confined with charged small molecules tannic acid and the amphiphilic molecule through cross‐linking and electrostatic modulation, respectively. The obtained membrane achieves ion selectivity ratios of 87 for K + /Mg 2+ , 74 for Na + /Mg 2+ , and 67 for Li + /Mg 2+ . The output power density can reach 30.2 W m −2 under a 50‐fold salinity gradient in osmotic energy harvesting, with a conversion efficiency of 43.8%. Furthermore, the membrane can be used in the chlor‐alkali process, enabling the production of high‐purity sodium hydroxide with brine containing divalent ions. This study provides a novel perspective for the development of next‐generation ion‐selective membranes, with potential applications in advanced resource and energy recovery technologies.

works.abstract: Using the Hansen’s solubility parameters (HSPs) approach, novel polyether block amide (PEBA)-polyethyl methacrylate (PEMA) polymer blend membranes were synthesized and applied for the pervaporation (PV) separation of 1-butanol. Blending with PEMA led to an increase in surface roughness and hydrophobicity. PV performance of the blend membranes for the recovery of 1-butanol from aqueous solution (20 g/L) at 40 °C showed an improvement in separation performance with the blending of PEMA; however, a higher blending ratio (≥ 8 wt%) significantly reduced PV performance due to phase separation. The membrane (PBPM-5) containing 5 wt% of PEMA achieved the best PV separation, yielding a flux of 0.19 kgm −2 h − 1 and a separation factor of 15.5, which is a 50% enhancement in flux and a twofold increase in the separation factor as compared to the pristine PEBA membrane. An increase in PV operation temperature and feed butanol content showed simultaneous enhancement in both the separation factor and flux for the PBPM-5 membrane. Separation of butanol from multicomponent mixture resulted in lower performance indicating the presence of strong coupling effect. This work shows the PV butanol separation capability of PEBA can be significantly enhanced through the judicious blending of small amount of PEMA polymer.

Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH‐dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Experiments verify pH‐dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH‐mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

works.abstract: Bio-based membranes offer inherent biodegradability and environmental compatibility, but their poor durability remains a major barrier to practical water purification. In this study, we propose a novel bioinspired dual-anchoring interfacial strategy for stabilizing a gelatin hydrogel as a functional layer on bacterial cellulose (BC) through a polydopamine (PDA) interlayer. The PDA interlayer binds to the BC nanofibers through hydrogen bonding of its catechol and amine groups, while its quinone sites form Schiff base linkages with the gelatin layer, which in turn provides the hydration barrier and the contact-active antibacterial function. The results indicated that the deposition time of the PDA interlayer is decisive. At a polymerization time of 12 h, a uniform PDA interlayer without visible aggregates was formed, which raised the gelatin fixation ratio from approximately 30% to over 90%. However, prolonged deposition (24 h) led to PDA particle aggregation, which increased surface heterogeneity and lowered gelatin retention. The optimized Gel-DA12-BC membrane rejects 88% of BSA at a permeance of 18 LMH bar −1 and sustains a flux recovery ratio of 94% over five filtration-cleaning cycles, and inhibits E. coli growth by approximately 72% without added biocides. These results establish that the durability of the composite is governed by the uniformity of the PDA interlayer rather than by the amount of PDA deposited, and that interfacial anchoring alone provides a fully aqueous, bio-based route to durable ultrafiltration membranes.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT High Mg/Li ratios and coexisting ions in salt‐lake brines limit the long‐term selectivity and structural stability of Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 (LATP) membranes. To address interfacial mass‐transfer resistance and Mg 2+ ‐induced performance decay, a graphite‐PVDF‐coated LATP membrane is constructed, enabling low‐resistance Li + transport while mitigating Mg 2+ interference. Under optimized conditions, the membrane increases Li + flux by ∼27% relative to pristine LATP, achieving a maximum Li–Mg separation factor of ∼6200 and a decreased water contact angle, indicating improved migration of hydrated Li + . Calculations show a lower Li + migration barrier in graphite than in LATP (0.27 vs. 0.68 eV), providing a low‐resistance pathway. Graphite also adsorbs Mg‐solvated clusters more strongly than Li‐solvated ones, reducing local Mg 2+ enrichment at the interface. DFT calculations suggest that Mg 2+ substitutes Ti/Al sites, lowering the Li + /H + exchange energy by 62.34 meV and reducing the Li/Mg migration‐barrier difference from 1.19 to 0.45 eV. HRTEM/SAED shows that the graphite‐PVDF layer mitigates lattice disorder, and TEM‐EDS reveals lower local Mg in the coated LATP after operation (0.23 vs. 0.49 wt.%). Long‐term tests show a ∼5‐fold longer service lifetime than the pristine membrane, providing insights into interfacial design for durable LATP‐based electrodialysis.

works.abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the use of a Li-selective membrane synthesized with the incorporation of hydrogen manganese oxide (HMO) to simplify the extraction process. The HMO-loaded membranes (HMOM) displayed remarkable performance for direct lithium extraction (DLE). The major accomplishments of incorporating HMO within the polymeric substrate were 2-fold. First, fast kinetics were observed for HMOM; ∼90% capacity (15 mg/g) was attained in 5 min in the filtration mode, with a pseudo-second-order kinetic rate constant (k2) ∼20 times higher as compared to the batch test, owing to enhanced mass transfer within the regulated channels of the membrane. Second, incorporation of HMO in the poly(ether sulfone) matrix reduced the Mn loss by five times and showed only &lt;0.2% Mn loss per cycle during the DLE from produced water (PW) matrix. We showed that the acid concentration can be reduced by 10 times for Li recovery, which further displayed an additional 4-fold decrease in Mn loss but led to a ∼10% decline in Li recovery performance. HMOM also demonstrated competitive selectivity for Li against competing cations within PW, with a separation factor of ∼20–40. We demonstrate a multipass, multistage filtration process as a framework for sequential DLE, concentration, and purification from real PW.

works.abstract: The integration of desalination and hydrogen production offers a promising pathway to simultaneously address water scarcity and clean energy demands. This study evaluated the feasibility and performance of coupled direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) and proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) systems for water–hydrogen cogeneration. A validated steady-state model was developed, incorporating coupled heat and mass transfer in DCMD and electrochemical, thermal, and hydrogen production models for PEMWE. A parametric analysis was conducted under two operational scenarios: (i) full coupling with zero net water output, and (ii) cogeneration of freshwater and hydrogen. The results indicate that system operation is constrained by the balance between DCMD production and PEMWE consumption, yielding a maximum current density of 2.29 A/cm² for a 50 cm² (1–2 kW) electrolyzer supported by a 200 cm² DCMD membrane. The net water production decreased from approximately 0.70 kg/h at zero current density to zero at this limit. The system efficiency decreased with increasing current density owing to rising activation and ohmic losses, as well as higher cooling requirements. By contrast, increasing stack temperature from 50 to 80 °C reduced cell voltage and improved overall efficiency, while lowering cooling demand. The feed temperature strongly enhanced the DCMD productivity, enabling higher feasible operating current densities. In the cogeneration mode, increasing the membrane area to 0.5 m² enabled simultaneous operation, with more than 95% of the produced water remaining available as useful output. These findings provide design insights for the development of water-efficient green hydrogen systems, particularly for deployment in water-limited regions

Here, we show that suitably chosen polyampholytic block copolymer grafting to the internal pore surfaces of CDI electrodes can substantially enhance CDI performance, via a combination of dipolar response and steric effects. Using mean-field classical density functional theory and grand-canonical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that such polymer grafted electrodes enable strongly improved desalination performance, without altering the pore width and geometry. Even an electrode grafting by simple neutral polymers can generate an improvement, although a suitably designed diblock polymer sequence offers an additional performance gain. These results establish interfacial block copolymer grafting as a powerful route toward high-performance, membrane-free desalination.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Pressure‐driven distillation (PD) has emerged as a transformative technology for harnessing non‐conventional water resources, leveraging hydraulic pressure to accelerate vapor generation and transport across vapor‐gap membranes. Despite its promise, the paradigm of conventional PD is fundamentally constrained by overlooked thermodynamic energy barrier, which severely limits overall process efficiency. Herein, we report the first conceptualization and fabrication of an ultra‐selective Janus vapor‐gap membrane engineered explicitly for PD, featuring a superhydrophilic, highly crystalline, and defect‐free covalent organic framework (COF) layer that decisively overcomes this limitation. The Janus membrane embodies a bilayered architecture with the upper layer functions as a vapor generation zone, sustaining a robust gas‐liquid interface for efficient evaporation, while the lower layer serves as a confined condensation zone that significantly reduces the energy barrier for vapor‐to‐liquid phase transition. This strategic spatial decoupling of evaporation and condensation enables a synergistic enhancement of the entire PD process. The resulting Janus membrane achieves near‐complete rejections of nonvolatile solutes. In practical desalination scenarios, it demonstrates outstanding anti‐fouling and chlorine resistance. This work not only highlights the potential of crystalline porous materials in PD technology, but also provides a pathway for architected Janus membranes that transcend the efficiency limits of conventional desalination processes.

works.abstract: Abstract Sequence-defined polymers provide unique opportunities to encode complex molecular functions through precise sequence control, yet independently programming molecular recognition and membrane interfaces within a single polymer architecture remains challenging. This limitation is particularly evident in artificial ion channels, where ion recognition is intrinsically coupled to channel architecture, requiring redesign of the membrane-spanning structure to target different ions. Here, we establish a sequence-defined DNA polymer platform that orthogonally programs ion recognition and membrane anchoring through independent control of nucleobase sequence and phosphorothioate backbone alkylation. The nucleobase sequence encodes the ion-recognition fold, whereas a fold-matched pattern of phosphorothioate backbone alkylation independently defines the membrane-facing surface. As a stringent demonstration of this design principle, we reprogrammed our previously reported K+-selective DNA channel into a silver ion channel (SIC) by replacing both the recognition chemistry and folding topology from a G-quadruplex to a stem-loop containing Ag+-binding metallo-base pairs, while preserving the orthogonal membrane-anchoring strategy. SIC selectively assembled in response to Ag+, inserted into lipid membranes, and transported Ag+ with no detectable transport of Na+ or K+, producing an Ag+ response more than 240-fold above the detection limit for the competing cations. A Watson–Crick control carrying the identical alkylation pattern but lacking Ag+-coordination sites was inactive, demonstrating that ion conduction proceeds through the sequence-encoded metallo-base-pair recognition axis rather than the alkylated polymer backbone. Together, these results establish orthogonal programming of ion recognition and membrane anchoring as a general molecular design strategy for sequence-defined DNA polymers, enabling programmable artificial ion channels with readily reconfigurable ion selectivity while providing a transferable design framework for future sequence-defined polymer systems.

works.title: Advanced Separation Technologies for Lithium Recovery from Brines: Performance, Economics and Sustainability
works.journal: The Sydney Journal of Interdisciplinary Engineering
works.abstract: Lithium carries the charge in the lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles (EVs), and demand for it is growing quickly. The International Energy Agency (IEA) expects about 23 million electric cars to be sold in 2026, and lithium demand could triple by 2040. Brines supply a large share of this lithium, as extraction from brine typically costs 30–50% less than mining hard rock. However, the conventional method of solar evaporation is slow, uses large amounts of water and only works on certain brines. Direct lithium extraction (DLE) offers an alternative. This review compares the three main DLE technologies, namely adsorption, membranes and electrochemical cells, along with the modelling and AI tools used to design them and the cost, sustainability and governance evidence that investors need. The Salar de Atacama in Chile is used as a case study. Most laboratory studies report high selectivity, but they use simplified brines, run for only a small number of cycles or hours, and stop at an enriched solution rather than a battery-grade product. Sorbents lose material, membranes foul, electrodes degrade, and reported energy figures often leave out pumping and regeneration. Evidently, selectivity or recovery alone cannot show which technology will be profitable. This review therefore recommends that investors compare technologies per kilogram of the same product, from pretreatment through to a specified purity. Before committing capital, investors should also ask for long trials on real brine, consistent reporting of water and energy use, and community participation. projectgroup13_458452_53577610_…

works.abstract: Abstract The development of battery separators derived from renewable feedstocks that can simultaneously achieve high porosity, robust mechanical strength, excellent thermal stability, reliable electrochemical performance, and satisfactory environmental sustainability remains a core challenge in the field of sustainable energy storage material. Herein, we report a regenerated cellulose membrane prepared through a dissolution/regeneration process using lithium bromide Molecular dynamics simulation results show that water is the effective antisolvent for driving the formation of cellulose–cellulose H-bonds, yielding cellulose with a better crystalline structure. Subsequently, tert-butanol was utilized to replace water in the cellulose membrane precursor prior to drying, preventing capillary-induced pore collapse. This membrane exhibits high porosity of 70.1%, excellent electrolyte uptake capacity of 243.7%, ionic conductivity of 0.77 mS/cm, excellent thermal stability (no shrinkage at 150 °C), and roust mechanical strength. The Na/HC half-cells assembled with this membrane displays high cycle capacity retention rate of 87.1% at 0.1 C after 500 cycles, which is comparable to commercial separators. This membrane fabrication process enables closed-loop solvent recycling, and the membrane fully degraded after 4 months of soil burial, and life cycle assessment indicated lower impacts than commercial battery separators. These results establish a practical closed-loop strategy for sustainable, high-performance battery separators.

works.abstract: Multi-effect distillation with thermal vapor compression (MED-TVC) is widely used for seawater desalination, but the mixing process in the steam ejector is associated with exergy destruction. This study investigates a six-effect MED system integrating turbine-driven mechanical vapor compression (MED-TDC), together with four selected feedwater preheating configurations. A steady-state model is developed to compare the energy, exergy, and exergoeconomic performance of the proposed systems with conventional MED-TVC. At a first-effect evaporation temperature of 60 °C, the baseline MED-TDC achieves a net gained output ratio (GOR) of 10.41, compared with 7.61 for MED-TVC, an increase of 36.9%. Among the four selected preheating configurations, TDC3 gives the highest net GOR of 10.87. Under the adopted nominal cost assumptions, MED-TVC has the lowest specific freshwater production cost of 1.175 $/m3, while TDC3 has the lowest value among the MED-TDC cases, at 1.194 $/m3. Within the explicitly resolved component boundary, the exergy-destruction sum is 398.26 MW for MED-TVC and 235.25–241.92 MW for the MED-TDC cases; the baseline MED-TDC has the lowest sum among the MED-TDC cases, whereas TDC3 has the highest. The results indicate that turbine-driven vapor compression increases net GOR under the reference conditions, while the selected feedwater arrangements produce configuration-dependent changes in component-level exergy destruction and nominal freshwater production cost.

works.title: Voltage-Gated Ionic Conductivity in Ultranarrow Confinement
institutions: Imperial College London
works.abstract: Abstract Voltage-controlled ion transport in subnanometer pores underpins the operation of emerging filtration, energy-storage, and iontronic technologies, yet its microscopic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate ionic transport in ultranarrow (≤1 nm) quasi-two-dimensional nanopores in MXene electrodes filled with an ionic liquid. We reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of linear-response conductivity on electrode potential, with a pronounced asymmetry between positive and negative electrode polarizations. These behaviors originate from a competition between confinement-induced ionic ordering and charging-induced ion crowding within the pore. The resulting transition from a structure-limited to an ion-crowding-limited transport regime provides a general framework for understanding voltage-gated ionic conduction under extreme confinement, which facilitates the formulation of design principles for MXene-based nanofluidic, electrochemical, and iontronic devices.

works.title: Boosting Oxygen Transport with Nanoporous Graphdiyne for High‐Capacity Li−O 2 Batteries
institutions: State Key Laboratory for Advanced Metals and Materials
University of Science and Technology Beijing
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Li−O 2 batteries have attracted extensive attention due to their potential to achieve several times higher energy density than Li‐ion batteries. However, the actual discharge capacity and rate performance still fall short of practical requirements, as cathodes made of dense carbon black particles hinder the fast diffusion of O 2 deep into the cathode during discharge, thus severely limiting cathode utilization. In this work, we introduce graphdiyne (GDY) into the cathode to accelerate O 2 transport. GDY is a two‐dimensional material with intrinsic nanopores that allow O 2 molecules to pass through. When incorporated into carbon‐black cathodes, GDY particles forms pathways of low diffusion resistance that facilitate O 2 diffusion deep into the cathode. The accelerated O 2 transport, which is supported by gas permeability measurement, enhances the discharge capacity of the battery by over 4 times to 10.36 mAh cm −2 , equivalent to 950 mAh g −1 (Li2O2+carbon) . Characterization of the discharged cathode reveals that GDY introduction substantially changes the growth of the discharge product, lithium peroxide, promoting its formation both in the form of larger particles and deeper throughout the cathode, thereby contributing to higher discharge capacity. Our findings demonstrate a new strategy for accelerating mass transport to improve cathodes utilization, and ultimately realizing high‐energy‐density Li−O 2 batteries.

works.title: Coordination‐Chemistry‐Directed Nanofluidic Ion‐Channel Engineering Enables Trimodal Self‐Powered, Colorimetric, and Wireless Humidity Transduction in a Wet‐Spun Biopolymer Fiber
institutions: Jiangnan University
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable humidity monitoring is central to personalized healthcare, yet few nanostructured platforms unite colorimetric, self‐powered, and wireless transduction within a single fiber. Here, a hydrochromic fiber is fabricated by wet‐spinning a sodium alginate (SA)/tricarboxylated bacterial cellulose (TBC) dope into a CoCl 2 coagulation bath. Shear‐aligned TBC nanorods form anisotropic ion‐transport nanochannels, while coordinated Co 2+ ions act as both ionic cross‐linkers and hydrochromic centers, switching reversibly between tetrahedral (blue, dry) and octahedral (pink, wet) geometries for naked‐eye humidity readout. Paired with Ag and Zn wire electrodes, the resulting galvanic cell delivers a peak open‐circuit voltage of ∼900 mV at 91% relative humidity (RH), a peak sensitivity of 13.75 mV %RH −1 , response/recovery times of 1.1/1.28 s, and stable operation over 200 wet–dry cycles across 10°C–70°C. Molecular dynamics simulations show that water uptake reorganizes the hydrogen‐bond network and drives Co 2+ /Cl − transport from a sub‐diffusive to a diffusive regime. Interfaced with a Bluetooth Low Energy microcontroller, the fiber enables real‐time wireless tracking of respiration, including sleep apnea events, and diaper‐wetness alerts; a Random Forest classifier discriminates six respiratory states with 99.2% accuracy in a single‐subject proof‐of‐concept test. This coordination‐chemistry strategy is transferable to other metal‐biopolymer systems.
